findings: The source boundary is correctly kept narrow: the repository only preserves doubly-linked-list insertion, while index-based insertion, zero-based indexing and [0,size] legality are explicitly declared candidate-contract choices.
The presented Java implementation is self-contained and covers empty, head, middle and tail insertion without undefined helpers or placeholder code.
The explanation states the bidirectional adjacency invariant and correctly separates O(1) pointer rewiring from O(min(index,size-index)) location cost for this chosen API.
The deterministic OpenJDK 21 fixture checks both traversal directions, reciprocal prev/next links, head/tail null boundaries, size updates and invalid indices against the candidate implementation.
Sentinel-node and already-known-node variants, concurrency limitations and project no-fabrication boundaries are explicitly handled rather than generalized beyond the source.
